handoff.purpose: Contains _contained_gate_child helper and command_gate factory function with extensive docstrings about containment setup and guarantees.

symbols.name: _contained_gate_child
symbols.note: Launches gate child at Low integrity; sets up worktree label, low temp dir, and append-only log; returns (proc, log).

symbols.name: command_gate
symbols.note: Factory returning a gate function that runs an arbitrary command inside candidate worktree with containment; handles cancellation, timeout, and refusal.

symbols.name: DEFAULT_GATE_TIMEOUT_S
symbols.note: Referenced but not defined in this chunk; assumed defined elsewhere.

claims.text: Launch the gate at Low integrity. Raises ContainmentUnavailable.
claims.why: The code calls containment.label_low_integrity and containment.spawn_contained but the actual raising of ContainmentUnavailable is not in this chunk; it may be raised by spawn_contained.

claims.text: THE WORKTREE IS LABELLED LOW, because a contained child that cannot write the tree it is testing is an outage, not a boundary.
claims.why: Code explicitly calls containment.label_low_integrity(worktree) on line 848.

claims.text: A LOW-LABELLED TEMP DIRECTORY, inside the gate's own scratch tree and NOT inside the worktree.
claims.why: Code creates low_temp = tmpdir / 'lowtemp' and labels it low; tmpdir is created in command_gate via tempfile.mkdtemp, which is not the worktree.

claims.text: THE OUTPUT FILE IS CREATED AND LABELLED BY US, then opened append-only, and exactly that one handle is allowlisted into the child.
claims.why: Code calls containment.open_low_append_log(out_path); the implementation details (labeling, append-only, allowlisting) are not in this chunk.

claims.text: THE GATE IS WHERE CANDIDATE CODE ACTUALLY RUNS. Everything else in this module handles the candidate's bytes; this command executes them. So by default the child is launched at LOW INTEGRITY through daedalus.spine.containment, and the kernel -- not our path checks -- refuses the writes that a Python guard provably cannot close (the 'move-in' attack among them).
claims.why: The code calls _contained_gate_child which labels worktree low and spawns contained; the kernel enforcement is out of scope but the intent is clear.

claims.text: THERE IS NO contained=False. A caller whose runner cannot produce candidate code says so with executes_candidate=False, which is a statement about the WORKLOAD and reads as one in a diff. A security toggle would read as a knob, and the first person in a hurry would turn it. When containment cannot be established -- wrong platform, labelling refused, a handle that would not verify -- the gate REFUSES: passed=False with the reason in the output and in the attestation. It never downgrades to an uncontained run that looks like a contained one.
claims.why: The function signature has executes_candidate parameter (not contained). On ContainmentUnavailable, it sets refusal and calls containment.refusal_attestation; no fallback to uncontained run is visible.

claims.text: Both children run inside a Job Object with KILL_ON_JOB_CLOSE, so a cancelled attempt kills the whole process TREE rather than the immediate child -- a leaked test process still writing into a worktree that is about to be removed is a correctness hazard, not untidiness.
claims.why: No Job Object creation or reference is present in this chunk; it must be inside containment.spawn_contained or elsewhere.

claims.text: Output goes to a file OUTSIDE the worktree: a pipe would deadlock on a chatty run while we are polling the cancel token instead of reading. Under containment that file is the ONE handle inherited by the child, opened append-only on a Low-labelled target and verified on the handle.
claims.why: The out_path is created inside tmpdir (which is not the worktree), but the handle verification and inheritance details are not in this chunk.

claims.text: That scratch directory is then removed through the GUARDED walker, not shutil.rmtree -- it lives in %TEMP% under a prefix named in this file while candidate code is running as this user, so it is a delete against attacker-reachable ground like every other delete in this system. See _remove_gate_tmpdir, which also records what the Job Object does and does not contain.
claims.why: The function _remove_gate_tmpdir is not defined in this chunk; removal logic is not shown.

observations.what: The function _contained_gate_child uses a bare except BaseException: which catches all exceptions including KeyboardInterrupt and SystemExit, potentially interfering with process termination.
command_gate docstring claims 'Both children run inside a Job Object with KILL_ON_JOB_CLOSE' but no such code is visible in this chunk; the claim is uncheckable.
The docstring references _remove_gate_tmpdir and guarded walker, but that function is not present in this chunk; its behavior cannot be verified.
The function command_gate defines _gate as inner function but does not show its full body; the chunk cuts off after the else clause.
The claim about 'refusal_attestation' function is uncheckable; it is called but not defined in this chunk.

The claim about 'output goes to a file OUTSIDE the worktree' is partially verifiable: out_path is inside tmpdir, which is created via tempfile.mkdtemp and is not the worktree. However, the exact location of tmpdir relative to worktree is not specified.
